title: Demographics of Close-In TESS Exoplanets Orbiting FGK Main-sequence Stars II. Spectral-Type Dependence and the Neptunian Landscape
comment: 21 pages, 17 figures, 10 tables, accepted for publication in MNRAS. Online interactive TESS occurrence rate: https://cuikaiming.com/TESS-SPOC-Occurrence-Rate/#fgk
summary: Understanding how planetary demographics depend on host star properties is essential for constraining planet formation and evolution theories. In this paper, we analyse close-in 0.5-16 d planet occurrence rates from the TESS Science Processing Operations Center (SPOC) full-frame image data for individual F-, G-, and K-type main-sequence stellar samples. Integrated over $0.5 < P < 16$ d and $2 < R_\mathrm{p} < 20\,R_\oplus$, the occurrence rates are $12.1^{+3.0}_{-2.3}$, $10.2^{+1.2}_{-1.0}$, and $13.1^{+1.4}_{-1.2}$ planets per 100 stars for F-, G-, and K-type hosts, consistent with each other at $1σ$, so any spectral-type dependence is localized rather than global. For transiting hot Jupiters, we measure $0.30^{+0.04}_{-0.03}$, $0.50\pm0.03$, and $0.67^{+0.08}_{-0.07}$ per cent, with the rate peaking at K type; the latter being the first such measurement for K-type hosts. Modelling the Neptunian desert directly in occurrence-rate space, we find that the desert extends to longer orbital periods around hotter stars. Integrating over the desert interior gives $0.069^{+0.045}_{-0.011}$, $0.093^{+0.046}_{-0.022}$, and $0.150^{+0.033}_{-0.026}$ planets per 100 stars, implying about one close-in planet in a hundred lies inside the desert, and the desert is roughly twice as populated around K- as around F-type hosts. A rigorous Bayesian model comparison for the $6$-$8\,R_\oplus$ strip indicates that a distinct Neptunian ridge is not required to explain the measurements.

title: Best Bulk Bennu (B3): Elemental compositions of aggregate samples from asteroid Bennu
summary: Ivuna-type (CI) carbonaceous chondrites have long served as proxies for the bulk Solar System composition due to their close agreement with solar photospheric abundances and enrichment in volatile elements relative to other chondrite classes. However, CI chondrites have been subject to terrestrial alteration, which may have modified their original mineralogies and redistributed aqueously mobile elements. NASA's OSIRIS-REx mission delivered pristine material from the carbonaceous asteroid Bennu, and initial analyses revealed close compositional similarities with CI chondrites. This provides a valuable opportunity to refine estimates of the bulk Solar System composition. We report concentrations of 63 elements in aggregate (bulk, unsorted) Bennu material (representing a combined mass of ~8 g) analyzed across four laboratories. Within analytical uncertainties, we find no statistically significant differences among aliquots of two aggregate samples that were homogenized into powders, or among subsamples (including two previously reported) of a non-homogenized aggregate sample. Nor do we find measurable variations among sample masses ranging from tens of milligrams to several grams. These findings indicate that the material returned from Bennu is well mixed at the aggregate scale. Combining all of the data, we derive an average bulk elemental composition that we term Best Bulk Bennu (B3). Comparison of B3 with an average CI chondrite composition shows excellent agreement within analytical uncertainties, confirming that terrestrial alteration of CI chondrites is effectively isochemical for non-highly volatile elements. B3 and the CI chondrite average composition compare similarly to solar photospheric composition. Thus, CI meteorites and returned samples of carbonaceous asteroids are the best available materials for estimating the bulk Solar System composition of non-highly volatile elements.

title: Discovery of activity on Main Belt Asteroid 6993 (1995 BJ4)
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, to be published in ApJ Letters
summary: We report the discovery of activity on asteroid 6993 (1995 BJ4) in the Zwicky Transient Facility (ZTF) alert stream data on UT 2026 August 5, with the help of machine learning. Visible activity can be seen as early as UT 2026 June 25. Activity on this outer-main belt object is likely not primarily driven by rotational instability, but rather is consistent with an impact event or sublimation based on several arguments. If this activity is sublimation driven, 6993 would be the largest known main belt comet (11.85 km), with the largest perihelion distance (2.853 au) and an unusually high geometric albedo of 0.166 $\pm$ 0.030. Asteroid 6993 should be monitored as it approaches perihelion in 2027 January to distinguish between activity mechanisms and understand its potential volatile inventory.

title: OGLE-2015-BLG-1395Lb: A Cold Sub-Saturn Mass Planet Orbiting an M Dwarf
comment: 25 pages, 9 figures (color), 4 tables, accepted for publication in AJ
summary: We present an analysis of the high-magnification microlensing event OGLE-2015-BLG-1395 and report the discovery of a sub-Saturn mass companion to the lens. Photometric coverage of the planetary anomaly in the light curve was obtained from the University of Tasmania's Harlingten 1.27m telescope. Additional data were obtained following the peak from several other observatories, allowing photometric calibration and color measurement of the source. Fits to the light curve reveal a companion with mass ratio of q = 0.00062 +/- 0.00007 and two degenerate solutions for the projected separation, s = 1.7 +/-0.1 or 0.59 +/-0.04 Einstein ring radii. Source and lens parameters are further constrained by Subaru and Keck adaptive optics (AO) imaging in 2016. Finite source effects and AO flux constraints allow us to determine the planet and host star parameters to better than a factor of 2. The system is an ~0.2 Jupiter-mass planet orbiting an ~0.25 solar mass (early-mid M-dwarf) main-sequence star in the Galactic disk, at a distance of ~2 kpc. The two degenerate solutions from the light curve both place the planet beyond the snow line. As a cold sub-Saturn around an M dwarf, OGLE-2015-BLG-1395Lb is in possible conflict with core accretion theory. Spitzer photometry from the time of the event is consistent with this conclusion, although highly uncertain due to faintness and crowding. The inferred relative proper motion of 9.4 mas/yr is consistent with a source star in the bulge and a lens in the disk, and predicts that the source and lens could be resolved a decade after the event.

title: The GAPS Programme at TNG LXXXI. The puzzle of the HeI absorption signal in the atmosphere of V1298 Tau b with GIARPS@TNG
comment: 20 pages, accepted for publication in A&A
summary: Atmospheric escape shapes close-in planets mostly in their first tens of Myr. The young V1298Tau system (10-30Myr) is a benchmark for investigating photoevaporation and planetary evolution at early stages. The metastable HeI near-infrared triplet is a key proxy for atmospheric escape. We aim to detect and characterise HeI in the extended atmosphere of V1298Taub. We analysed four transits over a 4-year baseline using GIARPS (GIANO-B + HARPS-N) at the Telescopio Nazionale Galileo. We re-derived the projected spin-orbit angle by modelling the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect. Using simultaneous optical and near-infrared high-resolution transmission spectroscopy of V1298Taub, we monitored the HeI triplet alongside key chromospheric indicators ($\log R'_{HK}$, H$α$, and NaI) to disentangle stellar activity from planetary evaporation. While the stellar spectra show significant night-to-night variability, transmission spectroscopy reveals persistent HeI absorption across all four epochs. This contrasts with H$α$ and NaI, observed over two nights with simultaneous HARPS-N monitoring, which fluctuate between emission and absorption due to stellar activity. The consistent presence of HeI over 4 years may suggest a planetary origin, despite stellar-driven depth modulation. ATES hydrodynamic simulations show that stellar XUV flux variations modulate the HeI absorption depth and equivalent width. Furthermore, stellar wind fluctuations likely drive the observed night-to-night variability of the exospheric structure. The detection of HeI across all epochs may support planetary evaporation, despite modulation by stellar activity. Our results underscore that disentangling a planetary signal from stellar contamination remains challenging for highly active hosts; securing the planetary nature of the HeI signature requires activity monitoring and full transit coverage to establish a robust baseline.

title: Diversity of planetary origins and compositions traced by stellar abundance differences of co-natal star systems
comment: Accepted by A&A, 11 pages, 3 figures, 3 pages appendix
summary: Co-natal stars, wide binaries that form from the same molecular cloud, should harbor the same stellar composition. Observations indicate stellar abundance differences in a small fraction of these co-natal systems. The stellar abundance differences have been attributed to the ingestion of planets by their host stars. We analyze a previous sample of co-natal stars to determine the composition of the planets that were ingested. The abundance differences in these co-natal pairs can show a positive abundance difference of the refractory elements (Fe, Mg, Si) paired with a positive, zero, or negative abundance difference of volatiles (O, C, S). Positive trends of refractory and volatile abundance differences can be explained (at minimum) with the ingestion of a single planet by one of the stars. Positive trends of refractory abundance differences paired with zero or negative abundance differences of oxygen and carbon imply that both stars are required to ingest planets formed at different locations (interior/exterior to the water and/or C-grain evaporation front). Some systems show a sulfur abundance difference that is a factor of a few lower than the abundance difference of Fe, Si, and Mg, even though sulfur is accreted via the moderately volatile compound FeS. This can be explained by the migration of one of the planets across the FeS evaporation front, where the planet first accretes large amounts of sulfur and then no sulfur, while still accreting the other refractory elements before being ingested by its host star. Our study shows that the planetary compositions derived from the detailed stellar abundances can explain the measured abundance differences of co-natal stars, giving a handle on the composition of exoplanets. At the same time it implies very different planetary compositions caused by the different formation location of these planets, in agreement with planet formation models.

title: The ALMA Survey of Gas Evolution of PROtoplanetary disks (AGE-PRO): Evolution of dust properties from multi-wavelength observations
comment: 14 pages, 11 figures. Accepted for publication in MNRAS, supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23535413
summary: Understanding the evolution of solids in protoplanetary discs is important to comprehend the formation of giant planets cores and terrestrial planets. The ALMA Large Program AGE-PRO studied key disc properties in a survey of 30 protoplanetary discs across three evolutionary stages: the embedded phase (0.5-1 Myr), the middle-age phase (1-3 Myr), and the end of the disc lifetime (2-6 Myr). Preliminary dust properties were estimated using 1.3 mm observations, but a multi-wavelength analysis provides a better constraint of important properties such as the dust disc mass, the dust temperature, and the maximum grain size. We present new ALMA 3.1 mm and 1.5 mm (Bands 3 and 5) continuum observations of the complete survey of 30 AGE-PRO discs. We fitted the observed visibilities and derived radial brightness profiles, spatially resolving 20 discs from the AGE-PRO sample at the two studied wavelengths. A multi-wavelength modelling was performed including also the radial profiles from the 1.3 mm observations. Our results replicate trends obtained from the single wavelength analysis: the dust disc size seems to be constant over age and the dust disc mass decreases with time, with a factor $\sim$10-40 uncertainty from opacity assumptions. This result implies much lower gas-to-dust mass ratios for the discs in our sample than previously reported. In addition, the derived spectral indices are consistent with optically thick emission in a large fraction of the AGE-PRO discs, in particular for the Ophiuchus and Lupus discs.

title: ExoVetter and a TESS Exoplanet Transit Search of Kepler Stars as Ground Truth
summary: We introduce a Python package called exoVetter that produces vetting metrics and visualizations to evaluate transiting exoplanet signals found in high-cadence time-series photometry. exoVetter is open source, modular, and independent of the mission data so that it can be easily expanded and used as part of different transit search pipelines tuned to different science cases and missions. We demonstrate its use in a pipeline as a way to distinguish real events found in a box-least squares exoplanet transit search of 324,530 light curves from the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite mission; we limit our demonstration to stars also observed by the more sensitive Kepler telescope as a way to establish ground truth for the events found in the light curves. Using this ground truth, we provide baseline thresholds for several flux-level vetters and one centroid-offset vetter when using exoVetter metrics on TESS data. Our demonstration also indicates that it is possible to create a planet catalog from the light curves of dim targets (>13.5Tmag) that has a similar fraction of real events to that of the bright targets (<13.5Tmag) for short period events identified in the TESS-Gaia light curves.

title: Comprehensive Visible and Near-infrared Keck and Gemini Monitoring and Characterization of Interstellar Comet 3I/ATLAS during its Encounter with the Solar System
comment: 53 pages, 21 figures, 9 tables. Submitted to AJ
summary: We present 14 optical imaging and eight optical spectroscopic epochs of interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS from Keck/LRIS and Gemini/GMOS, two near-infrared (NIR) imaging epochs from Keck/MOSFIRE, and four NIR spectroscopic epochs from Gemini/Flamingos-2 and GNIRS, obtained between 2025 July and 2026 May. Mean GMOS colors of $g-r=0.732\pm0.029$, $r-i=0.237\pm0.025$, and $i-z=0.109\pm0.022$ mag show no significant change across perihelion. Phase-corrected red-band activity follows $Afρ\propto r_h^{-2.10\pm0.14}$ inbound and $r_h^{-3.34\pm0.43}$ outbound. Transverse-width and sunward-plume speeds imply dust losses of $2.7\times10^9$ and $1.0\times10^{10}$ kg over 2025 July 3--2026 May 15 for 1-$μ$m--1-mm grains, equivalent to global layers of 0.26 and 0.99 m under the adopted grain and nucleus assumptions. The concentrated coma, compact sunward feature, and antisolar tail seen on 2025 August 27 broadened by 2025 November 26; extended dust persisted through 2026 February 17. C$_2$/CN nearly doubled from $0.257\pm0.014$ on 2025 September 14--15 to $0.481\pm0.080$ on 2025 November 26, while C$_3$/CN fell from $0.327\pm0.024$ on 2025 August 28 to $0.214\pm0.009$ on 2025 September 14--15. MOSFIRE NIR imaging on 2025 July 11 gives $Y-J=0.466\pm0.143$, $J-H=0.239\pm0.052$, $H-K_s=0.454\pm0.150$, and $J-K_s=0.693\pm0.202$ mag. Spectra give $J-H=0.24$ mag on 2025 September 5--6 and $J-H=0.27$--0.28 and $J-K_s=0.21$--0.22 mag on 2025 December 1--2 over the retained passband intervals. Model-calibrated imaging on 2026 February 6 gives near-solar $J-K_s=0.303\pm0.051$ mag. No water-ice absorption is robust to the tested continuum and calibration choices in the NIR spectra. These observations provide a lasting record of the comet's evolution through the Solar System and a benchmark for studying and monitoring future interstellar objects.
